key: As the birds fly forth from their resting places, so men with store of food rise at thy dawning.
s: Closing a hymn to the Dawn that praises her easy paths over hills and waters, the singer turns to the stir of morning; Sāyaṇa, on 6.64.6, reads the men who rise as those who share the offerings, or as those who earn their food.
src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 6.64.6, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 200403 (2019)

opened.locator: commentary on 6.64.6, and the hymn introduction

evidence.words: “ते तव “व्युष्टौ सत्यां “वयश्चित् पक्षिणोऽपि “वसतेः निवासस्थानात् “उत् “अपप्तन् उत्पतन्ति । "ये “पितुभाजः हविषां संभक्तारः अन्नस्योपार्जका वा । ‘ पितुः । इत्यन्ननामसु पाठात् । "नरः तेऽपि च उत्पतन्ति ।
evidence.gloss: At thy dawning, even the birds fly up from their dwelling place. The men who are pitubhāj, sharers of the oblations or earners of food (for pitu is read among the names of food), they too rise up.
evidence.licence: public domain text; transcription CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource)

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, ref 6.64.6, at [504,6]), first whole sentence of the last verse of the hymn. Sāyaṇa on 6.64.6 glosses pitubhājaḥ as haviṣāṃ saṃbhaktāraḥ (sharers of the oblations) or annasya upārjakāḥ (earners of food), citing pitu among the names of food, and says these men too rise; Wilson follows the second option. The sentence gives both alternatives with or, as he does. Plain sense faithful: 6.64 is a six-verse Uṣas hymn (introduction), 6.64.1 and 6.64.4 praise her easy paths on the hills and through waters, and 6.64.6 closes it; no four words of the key repeated.
